unit.title: Compiler Front-End Engineering Kickoff: A Tiny Expression Language
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student building practical software-engineering habits
prerequisites: Comfort reading algorithms and basic Java
learning_outcomes: Turn a small language contract into an ANTLR 4 grammar and Java front end
Make precedence, associativity, full-input consumption, and error behavior explicit
Separate generated parser code from authored application code
Build a deterministic command-line interface and repeatable automated tests
Explain design and testing decisions with evidence from the implementation
in_scope: Lexing and parsing a specified expression language
Pinned build dependencies, clean-build instructions, and automated tests
A short design note and written comprehension responses
out_of_scope: Optimization, runtime environments, and register allocation
Reproduction of an official NJU assignment
Completion of the full NJU Compilers course

unit_completion_requires: All required learner deliverables exist in the learner submission
A harness-controlled validator executes the documented clean build and tests
Observed behavior satisfies the examiner-only rubric and its critical gates
Written responses are evaluated against implementation evidence
evidence_sources: The submitted grammar, Java source, tests, build metadata, design note, and responses
completion_policy.failure_policy: Preserve failed-attempt evidence; a later attempt must be validated independently

provenance.source_use: Catalog metadata informed scope and tool choice; it was not treated as lesson content or an official unit sequence.
